summary.text: Metabolism is the set of life-sustaining chemical reactions that happen inside living organisms.
Its three main jobs are turning food energy into a usable form, turning food into building blocks for large molecules, and getting rid of metabolic wastes.
The reactions are organized into pathways, where a series of steps, each helped by a specific enzyme, turns one chemical into another.

facts.label: Catabolic reactions
facts.value: Break compounds down, and usually release energy

facts.label: Anabolic reactions
facts.value: Build up compounds, and usually consume energy

facts.label: Shared pathways
facts.value: Citric acid cycle acids are present in all known organisms

facts.label: Basal metabolic rate
facts.value: Measures the energy consumed by all these chemical reactions

facts.label: Name origin
facts.value: From a Greek word meaning change

items.prompt: A cell splits glucose into pyruvate during cellular respiration. How is this reaction best described?

options.label: Building up a compound, which usually consumes energy
Breaking down a compound, which usually releases energy
Breaking down a compound, which usually consumes energy
Building up a compound, which usually releases energy

items.explain: Breaking compounds down is called catabolism, and catabolism usually releases energy.

items.prompt: A growing cell stitches amino acids together into new proteins. Which kind of reaction is this, and what usually happens to energy?

options.label: Catabolic, and energy is usually released
Catabolic, and energy is usually consumed
Anabolic, and energy is usually released
Anabolic, and energy is usually consumed

items.explain: Building up compounds such as proteins is anabolism, and anabolism usually consumes energy.

items.prompt: A cell converts chemical A into chemical D, passing through B and C along the way. How is this kind of conversion organized in metabolism?

options.label: As a pathway where each stage is helped by its own specific enzyme
As one enzyme that performs the whole conversion in a single move
As a free-for-all in which no particular enzymes take part
As a pathway where the enzymes are used up at every stage

items.explain: Metabolic reactions form pathways in which one chemical becomes another through a series of steps, each helped by a specific enzyme.

items.prompt: A reaction a cell needs will not happen by itself because it requires energy. How can the cell still drive it?

options.label: Simply wait, because given enough time it will start by itself
Remove the enzymes so that nothing interferes with the reaction
Use an enzyme to couple it to a spontaneous, energy-releasing reaction
Raise the basal metabolic rate until the reaction begins to run

items.explain: Enzymes let organisms drive reactions that need energy by coupling them to spontaneous reactions that release energy.

items.prompt: Hydrogen sulfide gas feeds some prokaryotes but is poisonous to some animals. What best explains the difference?

options.label: The gas changes its chemistry depending on which species meets it
Each organism's metabolic system decides what it finds nutritious
Prokaryotes are protected from every poison by their small size
Animals cannot make any hydrogen sulfide of their own at all

items.explain: The metabolic system of an organism determines which substances it finds nutritious and which poisonous.

items.prompt: E. coli and elephants are very different, yet both have the same set of carboxylic acids in their citric acid cycle. What does this suggest?

options.label: Elephants picked up the cycle from bacteria in recent times
The two species built the cycle independently by pure chance
Only this one cycle is shared, while all other pathways differ
Basic pathways likely appeared early and were kept because they work

items.explain: Basic metabolic pathways are similar across very different species, likely because they appeared early and were retained due to their efficacy.
